title: Establishment of a biobank for research into the role of the intestinal and oral microbiome in the development of diseases of the digestive tract
summary:
The intestinal microbiome varies from person to person and changes in composition along the gastrointestinal tract. While the number of microorganisms in the stomach is still relatively small, their number is several orders of magnitude higher in the large intestine. The microbiome regulates important physiological processes such as the maturation of the intestinal immune system and the digestion of nutrients. On the other hand, changes in the composition or activity of the microbiome can contribute to intestinal inflammation and tumor development. The gut microbiome also appears to influence the function of organs outside the intestine, such as the lungs and brain. The microbiome is influenced by a variety of factors, including diet and exercise. 

The ColoBAC biobank contains, among other biological samples, stool, saliva, and mucosa samples for research into the gastrointestinal system with the focus on the microbiome in healthy individuals as well as in the context of diseases of the digestive tract. In addition, lifestyle factors and disease data (e.g., medications) can be examined together with the microbiome and the disease in order to address the complex interaction between the microbiome, disease, and humans. The aim of the study is to better understand this complex interaction and to discover gut microbial signatures that can be used in a safe manner for preventive and diagnostic purposes.
conditions: Alterations and diseases of the digestive tract/gastrointestinal system (e.g. in the context of diseases corresponding to ICD-10 dialogue such as K51, K50, C18 or E66) and axis from the intestine (microbiome) to peripheral organs (e.g. in the context of diseases corresponding to ICD-10 dialogue such as K58)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who have a disease of the gastrointestinal system, who are suspected of having a disease of the gastrointestinal system, and/or who require endoscopic examination (colonoscopy and/or esophagogastroscopy) for further clarification, or who are presenting for an endoscopic check-up or preventive examination.
Exclusion criteria:
- Inability to consent to the study
- Contraindication to biopsy sampling
- Patients in reduced general condition (ECOG > 2)
